messages:
marie: Heads-up — I want to add a UNIQUE index on users(email). Target Wed 2026-04-07 02:00 UTC. We expect about a 30m maintenance window where we will run a short dual-write flag to avoid downtime. Who can own the deploy and the smoke checks?

raj: I can run the deploy. Plan: canary to 10% of traffic first, then full. Are we doing CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY or a table-swap approach?

callie: Prefer background backfill + swap to avoid long locks. Workflow I'd follow:
1) create new column users.email_norm
2) backfill normalized emails in background job
3) dedupe duplicates (keep oldest id)
4) create unique index on email_norm
5) flip feature flag to use email_norm

Example dedupe SQL I'll run:
```
WITH dupes AS (
  SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lower(email) ORDER BY created_at) AS rn
  FROM users
)
DELETE FROM users WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM dupes WHERE rn > 1);
```

tim: SRE here — I'll reserve the duration on the maintenance calendar and be on-call for rollback. Make sure runbook has exact DB host list and psql commands. I also want a quick smoke list.

marie: Smoke checks (canary & post-deploy):
- signups (happy path)
- login by email
- password reset emails
- admin user lookup by email
- query latency p50/p95 for users_by_email

raj: Got it. I'll run canary at 02:00 UTC, wait 10m, then promote. I'll also tag the deploy with git sha and post the migration script in the PR. My deploy commands:
```
-- run backfill job
psql -h db-ro 'db' -f migrations/2026xxxx_add_email_norm.sql
-- create index
psql -h db-primary 'db' -c "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_users_email_norm ON users(lower(email_norm));"
```

olga: Heads-up from data: backfill will touch ~3M rows; estimate 18–25 minutes on replica. Keep IO throttling optional. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Migration job scheduled by @raj for 2026-04-07T02:00:00Z. Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/migrations/email-uniq

sre-oncall: Rollback plan:
- disable feature flag `use_email_norm`
- DROP INDEX if it created incorrectly (use pg_terminate_backend if needed) — prefer not to
- restore from replica snapshot if catastrophic (last resort)
I'll create a small rollback script and keep it handy in the runbook.

marie: Perfect. @callie can you own the dedupe job timing and confirm it's completed by Tue 23:00 UTC so we have a dry-run? If anything blocks, post here. :thumbsup:

callie: Yup — I'll run dry-run Mon night and report results by Tue EOD. Will open PR with backfill metrics.

raj: I'll post the canary logs and smoke summary to this thread after the deploy.

marie: Thanks everyone. I'll update the calendar invite and add the outage details to the release notes. If pause needed, we'll abort during canary.

sre-oncall: I'll be monitoring alerts and will ping if any DB errors spike. Good to go from my side.
